references.text: Prohibition against spreading false rumors, which expands on the ban against going about as a slanderer among the people.
Whoever goes about as a slanderer reveals secrets. Proverbs warns against the backbiter who discloses confidential information.
Warns against associating with one who reveals secrets and with someone who has a loose tongue, linked to the prohibition against gossip.
Ezekiel condemns slanderers who shed blood, connecting gossip with violence and guilt of bloodshed.
Jeremiah describes how the people go about as slanderers and deceive one another, a direct violation of this commandment.
Exhortation to rescue those being led away to death, linked to the prohibition against standing passively when your neighbor's life is in danger.
Reuben tried to save Joseph from being killed by his brothers, a positive example of not standing passively while one's neighbor's blood is shed.
James warns against slandering one another, a New Testament parallel to the prohibition against gossip.
Jesus teaches that people will have to give an account for every careless word they speak, linked to responsibility for speech.
